title: Ommesh history file, version 1
description: The chats, contacts and messages of one MeshCore radio, as Ommesh saves them to a file and brings them in from one. See docs/history-format.md. Readers ignore fields they do not know.

version.description: Raised only when a reader of the old version would read the file wrong.

app.description: What wrote the file, with its version.

radio.description: The radio whose history this is. Ommesh brings a file in only to this radio.

time.description: RFC 3339, written in UTC with a Z.

key.description: A node's whole public key, 32 bytes in hex. Written lower-case.

keyStart.description: The first bytes of a node's public key, in hex, as messages name their senders.

path.description: The relays a packet went through, first relay first, each as the hash it signs the path with. All hashes of one path have the same size.

on.description: radio: the radio held it. removed: taken off the radio, kept to be put back. heard: its advert was heard but the radio did not keep it. radio when absent.

removedBy.description: For a removed contact: by hand, by the tidy-up rule, or by the radio itself.

flags.description: The contact's flags byte as MeshCore firmware keeps it; bit 0 is a favourite. 0 when absent.

lastAdvert.description: When its last advert was sent, by the node's own clock.

lastHeard.description: When it was last heard, by the clock of the device that kept the history.

route.description: The route the radio held to it. null: none, the next message floods. Empty: a neighbour reached direct.

chat.description: The chat a message is in: a channel by its secret, a node by its key, or a sender the radio could not name by the start of its key.

id.description: Kept as it is. Two messages are the same when chat, direction, sentAt to the second, sender and text match, whatever their ids.

text.description: On a channel, without the sender's name in front.

sentAt.description: By the sender's clock, which can be far off.

receivedAt.description: When it came in or was written, by the clock of the device that kept the history. sentAt when absent.

from.description: Who sent a message that came in. On a channel only the name is known; in a room, the author of the post.

roomPost.description: A post a room server relayed, signed by its author.

snr.description: How well the radio heard it, dB.

hops.description: Relays it passed on its way in.

status.description: For an out message. queued: written while the radio was away. sending: waiting for an acknowledgement. sent: gone; on a channel, a repeater was heard sending it on. delivered: acknowledged. unheard: on a channel, no repeater was heard sending it on. unconfirmed: no acknowledgement came. failed: it could not go.

route.description: An out direct message: the relays it went along.

echoes.description: Copies the radio heard, one per path: of an out channel message, repeaters sending it on; of one that came in, each copy that reached the radio.
